<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]; [[Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict]]
**A [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-led coalition begins a [[military offensive]] against the [[Houthis]], carrying out [[airstrike]]s against the capital [[Sanaa]], as well as the [[Provinces of Saudi Arabia|provinces]] of [[Ma'rib Governorate|Ma'rib]], [[Al Jawf Governorate|al-Jawf]], [[Al Bayda Governorate|al-Bayda]], [[Hajjah Governorate|Hajjah]] and [[Saada Governorate|Saada]]. The local news describe the airstrikes as "violent" and reports scores of people injured. This is said to be the response to missile and [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] attacks against [[Saudi Arabia]] from last week to last night. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-saudi/saudi-led-coalition-starts-military-operation-against-yemens-houthis-idUSKBN2426FU?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Irapuato massacres]]
**Gunmen kill at least 24 people in a [[mass shooting]] at a [[drug rehabilitation]] center in [[Irapuato]], [[Guanajuato]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-violence/24-people-killed-in-attack-in-central-mexico-media-reports-idUSKBN2427M4 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Oromia Clashes]]
**An [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|Ethiopian military]] crackdown on protests in [[Oromia Region]] leaves 81 protesters dead, while several prominent politicians, such as [[Jawar Mohammed]], have been detained. The protests began following the death of [[Oromo people|Oromo]] musician [[Hachalu Hundessa]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-53243325 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Removal of Confederate monuments and memorials]], [[List of monuments and memorials removed during the George Floyd protests]]
**The [[Stonewall Jackson Monument|monument]] of [[Confederate States of America|Confederate]] General [[Stonewall Jackson]] is removed from [[Monument Avenue]] in [[Richmond, Virginia]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/richmond-orders-removal-confederate-statues-city-land-71561398 (ABC News)]
*[[Weinstein effect]], [[Fox News controversies]]
**[[Fox News]] fires ''[[America's Newsroom]]'' anchor [[Ed Henry]] following allegations of sexual misconduct by a former employee. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/07/01/media/ed-henry-fired-fox-news/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Finnish Air Force]] Command formally ends the use of the [[swastika]] in its imagery, according to the Air Force Command. However, the swastika will remain on some Air Force unit flags and decorations. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53249645 (BBC News)]
*The [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]], responding to recent criticism about the lack of [[racial diversity]] among the nominees in major [[Academy Awards|Oscar]] award categories, invites 819 people to become new members. Of the invitees, 49% are from outside the US, 45% are women, and 36% are non-white. [https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-53247124 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[Governor of California|California Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] restricts the indoor operations of certain businesses in 19 [[counties of California|counties]] for a minimum of three weeks to stop the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-07-01/newsom-imposes-new-rollbacks-of-californias-coronavirus-reopening (''Los Angeles Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania]]
****[[List of governors of Pennsylvania|Pennsylvania Governor]] [[Tom Wolf]] says that [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|masks]] will be required inside and outside. [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/505494-pennsylvania-issues-order-requiring-people-to-wear-masks-in-public (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio]]
****[[Dayton, Ohio|Dayton]] becomes the first city in [[Ohio]] to mandate masks. [https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/2020/07/01/coronavirus-ohio-dayton-first-major-ohio-city-mandate-masks/5359530002/ (Cincinnati.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****[[Miami-Dade County, Florida|Miami-Dade County]] is expected to mandate masks as it deals with surging cases. [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/coronavirus/article243931932.html (''Miami Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***The COVID-19 death toll in [[Brazil]] passes 60,000. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-brazil-tally/brazil-coronavirus-death-toll-passes-60000-as-pandemic-worsens-in-south-midwest-idUSKBN2427EB (Reuters)]
**The [[United Nations Security Council|UN Security Council]] demands "immediate cessation of hostilities" in conflict zones around the world, due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. These "durable humanitarian pauses", which do not apply to military operations against [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] and [[Al-Qaeda]], should begin immediately and be for at least 90 consecutive days to allow for delivery of humanitarian assistance and medical evacuations. This is the first resolution related to the COVID-19 pandemic that the council has passed. [https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/07/01/886079785/u-n-security-council-demands-cease-fire-in-conflict-areas-due-to-covid-19 (NPR)]

;International relations
*[[France–Turkey relations]]
**[[France]] suspends its involvement in [[NATO]]'s naval operation in the [[Mediterranean Sea]] enforcing an [[arms embargo]] on [[Libya]], following an investigation into an incident between French and [[Turkish Navy|Turkish]] [[warship]]s. France accuses the [[Turkish Naval Forces]] of harassing its [[French frigate Courbet|''Courbet'']] warship, while attempting to inspect a Turkish civilian vessel suspected of breaching the arms embargo. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/200701141138500.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations]], [[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] says up to three million [[Hong Kong]] residents will be offered citizenship in the [[United Kingdom]], following the passing of a controversial new [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|national security law]] by [[China]]. Under the British government's plans, Hong Kongers will be able to settle in the UK for five years under political asylum, and after a further year will be able to apply for citizenship. Foreign Secretary [[Dominic Raab]] says there will be "no limits on numbers or quotas", due to the UK's "historic commitment to the people of Hong Kong". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-53246899 (BBC News)]
*[[Foreign relations of Taiwan]], [[Foreign relations of Somaliland]]
**[[Taiwan]] announces it will mutually establish representative offices with the unrecognized [[breakaway state]] of [[Somaliland]]. While relations are not diplomatic at this point, further establishment of [[diplomatic relations]] would make Taiwan the first [[sovereign state]] to recognize Somaliland and the first new diplomatic ally that Taiwan has gained in 13 years. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-07-01/taiwan-to-set-up-representative-office-in-breakaway-somaliland (Bloomberg News)]

;Law and crime
*[[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**Police in [[Hong Kong]] arrest over 300 people on the previously banned [[Hong Kong 1 July marches|1 July march]] and after the passing of the new [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|national security law]]. The new law punishes crimes considered as [[subversion]], [[terrorism]] and [[collusion]] with foreign forces with up to [[life in prison]]. It also allows [[extradition]] to the [[Mainland China|Mainland]] for trial. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests/hong-kong-police-arrest-nearly-200-in-first-protest-under-new-security-law-idUSKBN2423Y2?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Censorship in Turkey]]
**[[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] vows tighter control over "immoral" [[social media]] following alleged insults to his daughter and son-in-law when they announced the birth of their fourth son on [[Twitter]]. Erdoğan specifically mentioned Twitter, [[YouTube]] and [[Netflix]]. Interior Minister [[Süleyman Soylu]] announced the arrest of a number of social media users for "insulting tweets". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/turkey-erdogan-vows-social-media-controls-insults-family-200701112027760.html (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Guardia di Finanza]] seizes over $1.2 billion (~[[Euro|€]]1 billion) worth of [[fenethylline]] tablets at a port in [[Salerno]], [[Campania]], [[Italy]]. It is believed that the [[amphetamine]]s were manufactured by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] and originated in [[Syria]]. The haul, amounting to 14 [[metric tonne]]s of contraband, is the largest drug bust in history. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/01/europe/isis-drug-seizure-italy-scli-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;Sports
*After hospitalization in intensive care due to a sudden [[immune system disorder]] during a training camp in [[France]], the situation of Dutch world champion [[short track speed skater]] [[Lara van Ruijven]] becomes critical. [https://nos.nl/l/2338946 (NOS)] [https://www.telegraaf.nl/sport/1704556717/toestand-van-ruijven-verslechtert-ze-vecht-voor-haar-leven (''Telegraaf'')]
